newsitem.title: USA: One woman killed as violent weather hits N.Dakota.
newsitem.headline: One woman killed as violent weather hits N.Dakota.

text.p: One woman was killed and two people were injured as a slow-moving front produced violent thunderstorms, high winds and hail overnight in North Dakota, officials said Thursday.

Vic Jensen, a meteorologist with the National Weather Service (NWS), said an elderly woman died when high winds destroyed a farmhouse in southern Renville County. Local officials said two other people were also injured when the structure was destroyed.
Jensen said the NWS was unable to confirm reports of a tornado touching down north of Minot.
"We can't confirm the tornado, (but) Minot Air Force Base had a wind gust of 126 miles per hour," Jensen said. "That tied a state record for the highest recorded wind speed."

A wind gust of 90 miles per hour was recorded in Granville, and hail and up to four inches of rain also hit parts of north central North Dakota, Jensen said. A spokesman at Minot Air Force Base said some sheet metal on the outside of the control tower was damaged by the high winds.
Meteorologists said the front had not completely moved through the state and that more severe weather was expected Thursday.
